# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17 (Bi-Vb Pc17)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17 (known as *Anāpucchāsantharaṇa*, "Putting out bedding without permission") is a monastic disciplinary rule belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule proscribes a nun from spreading out bedding in a house and then sitting or lying down on it without first requesting permission from the owners, an offense entailing expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. As noted by Ute Hüsken, this training rule forms part of a thematic sequence alongside Bhikkhunī Pācittiyas 15 and 16 addressing conduct when visiting lay households in the afternoon (*pacchābhattaṁ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā*), specifically curbing overly familiar behavior and violations of guest etiquette [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule was preserved across the Vinayas of multiple early Buddhist schools [SuttaCentral]. Parallels exist in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda (in both Chinese and Tibetan versions), Mahāsāṅghika, and the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda Vinaya [SuttaCentral]. Internally, DharmaNexus records extensive formulaic text reuse with adjacent and related sections of the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, most heavily with Pācittiya 16 (§1.17–2.1.13 ↔ §1.12–2.1.13) and Pācittiya 15 (§1.18–2.1.9 ↔ §1.17–2.1.9), as well as Pācittiyas 94, 13, and 12, the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* subcommentary (*Tika Vin04t*), and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Tibetan monastic commentaries, including the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-3) [DharmaNexus].
